mainTopic: Who receives the priestly gifts and how a כהן should take them, teaching an unworthy student, and marking a shared animal
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ברייתא listing the services every כהן must accept. From its wording, the גמרא infers that a כהן loses his gifts only by rejecting these services, not by lacking expertise, and uses this to challenge רב חסדא. רב rules that a כהן who cannot remove the forbidden veins from the jaw should not get it, but the גמרא rejects this, since the blood drains out however the jaw is prepared. רבא then reports רב יוסף's question about a כהן who grabs his gifts, and he answers from ״וְנָתַן״ that the gifts must be given, not taken. אביי describes how he grew step by step from grabbing, to asking, to only accepting, to refusing, except on ערב יום כיפור. רב יוסף allows a כהן to give his expected gifts to a poor תלמיד חכם. A story about רבא, רב ספרא and a dream shows the limits of that rule. The גמרא then explains the plain meaning of the dream פסוק as teaching an unworthy student, which רב condemns harshly. Finally, the גמרא returns to the משנה's rule about marking an animal shared with a כהן or a גוי, and raises a contradiction from a ברייתא; the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The list of Temple services every כהן must accept
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its list of priestly services. It derives from the words 'מבני אהרן' that a כהן must accept every service given to the sons of Aaron.
steps.simpleTranslation: The list continues: receiving the blood, sprinkling it, giving the סוטה the water to drink, breaking the neck of the עגלה ערופה, purifying the מצורע, and lifting the hands for ברכת כהנים, whether inside the Temple or outside it. The verse says 'from the sons of Aaron', which teaches that this applies to any service said about the sons of Aaron.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the ברייתא in the middle of its list of jobs that only a כהן does. It ends by giving the verse that this whole list comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא wants to show that a כהן must accept every priestly service, not just the sacrifices. The word 'מבני אהרן' widens the rule to include any job the Torah gives to the sons of Aaron, even jobs done outside the Temple, like ברכת כהנים. The גמרא is bringing this ברייתא so it can use it as a source against רב חסדא in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Receiving the blood of a sacrifice in a vessel
Giving the special water to a wife suspected of being unfaithful
The calf whose neck is broken when a murdered body is found and the killer is unknown
The purification ceremony for a person with צרעת
Lifting the hands for ברכת כהנים

phrases.english: and receivings of the blood, sprinklings,
and giving the sotah to drink,
and breaking the neck of the heifer,
and the purification of a leper,
and the lifting of the hands —
whether inside or outside the Temple,
the verse states: "from the sons of Aaron" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:33

phrases.english: any service that is stated about the sons of Aaron.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that was brought just before this section
steps.raayaObject: That a כהן must accept every service given to the sons of Aaron
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words מבני אהרן (ויקרא 7:33), as taught in the ברייתא

steps.title: Rejecting the services loses the gifts, but lacking expertise does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the ברייתא that only a כהן who rejects the services loses his share. A כהן who accepts them but is not expert still gets gifts, and this challenges רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says that any כהן who does not accept it has no share in the priesthood. The reason is that he does not accept it. So if he does accept it, he gets a share, even if he is not an expert in these services.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא very carefully and draws an inference from its exact wording. That inference is used as a challenge to רב חסדא's earlier ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא names only one thing that makes a כהן lose his share: not accepting (מודה) the services. The גמרא infers that a כהן who accepts them keeps his share even without being expert (בקי). That goes against רב חסדא, who had said a כהן who is not expert does not receive gifts.

keyTerms.meaning: Accepts or believes in (here, accepts the priestly services as valid)
He has no share in the priesthood (he gets no priestly gifts)
The reason; this word opens an inference from exact wording
But (if the case were different); introduces the opposite case

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'מודה' (accepting that the services are valid) with 'בקי' (knowing how to do them). The whole challenge rests on the difference between these two words.

phrases.english: And any priest who does not accept it —
has no portion in the priesthood.
phrases.notes: 'Portion' here means the gifts that כהנים receive.

phrases.english: The reason is that he does not accept it,
but if he accepts it —

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאֵינוֹ בָּקִי בָּהֶן.
phrases.english: he gets a portion even though he is not expert in them.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּאֵינוֹ מוֹדֶה בָּהּ, הָא מוֹדֶה בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא quoted in step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that a כהן who is not expert does not receive gifts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא names only rejecting the services as the cause for losing gifts, which implies that lacking expertise is not a cause.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the ברייתא, a כהן loses his gifts only if he rejects the priestly services, not merely because he lacks expertise.

steps.title: Do not give the jaw to a כהן who cannot remove its veins
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that the veins in the jaw are forbidden. So the jaw, which is one of the priestly gifts, is not given to a כהן who does not know how to remove them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of רב הונא, who said in the name of רב: The veins in the jaw are forbidden. We do not give the gift to any כהן who does not know how to remove them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling of רב about a specific kind of כהן who should not get a gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The jaw (לחי) is one of the gifts given to a כהן. Its veins hold blood, so they are forbidden to eat. רב worries that a כהן who does not know how to take them out will eat them, so he should not be given the jaw.

keyTerms.meaning: The jaw, one of the gifts given to a כהן

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Rav Huna said that Rav said:
The veins that are in the jaw are forbidden,
and any priest who does not know how to remove them —
we do not give him the gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling on the related topic of which כהן receives gifts
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The veins in the jaw are forbidden, and a כהן who cannot remove them is not given the jaw.

steps.title: The blood drains out anyway, so there is no worry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב's concern. Whether the jaw is roasted, or cut and salted before cooking, the blood drains out by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. If he roasts the jaw, the blood drains out. If he puts it in a pot, he first cuts it and salts it, and then the blood drains out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says רב's worry is not real and explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's concern was that the כהן would eat the blood in the veins. The גמרא points out that both normal ways of preparing meat remove the blood. Roasting over fire draws it out, and cutting and salting before cooking also draws it out. So the כהן's lack of knowledge causes no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: But that is not so; a rejection of the previous statement

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא rejects רב's rule. However the jaw is prepared, the blood drains out, so there is no reason to keep the gift from a כהן who does not know how to remove the veins.

phrases.english: But that is not so,
if it is roasted, the blood drains out,
and if it is for the pot —
if he cuts them and salts them —
the blood drains out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב's ruling from step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the worry behind רב's rule, and with it the rule that we do not give the gift
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The worry is not real, because every normal way of preparing the jaw removes the blood.

steps.title: רב יוסף's test: is grabbing the gifts good or bad?
steps.stepSummary: רבא reports that רב יוסף tested his students: when a כהן grabs the מתנות, is he showing love for the מצוה or disrespect for it?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רב יוסף tested us. A כהן who grabs the gifts, is he showing love for the מצוה, or is he treating the מצוה lightly?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: how a כהן should receive his gifts. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides make sense. Grabbing could show eagerness to do the מצוה, or it could show that the כהן is treating a holy gift like ordinary food he can just take.

keyTerms.meaning: The gifts: the foreleg, jaw and maw given to a כהן
Showing love and eagerness for a מצוה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: בָּדַק לַן רַב יוֹסֵף,
phrases.english: Rava said: Rav Yosef tested us,
this priest who grabs the gifts:
is he showing love for the מצוה,
or is he showing disrespect for the מצוה?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בָּדַק לַן רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who deserves the gifts to how a כהן should receive them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a כהן who grabs the gifts doing a praiseworthy act of eagerness or a disrespectful one?

steps.title: The gifts must be given, not taken
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers from the פסוק ״וְנָתַן״: the owner must give the gifts. The כהן may not take them on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I answered him: The Torah says 'and he shall give', which means he should not take them by himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רב יוסף's question using a word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says the owner ״וְנָתַן״, gives. The מצוה is an act of giving, so a כהן who grabs takes away the owner's part. That makes grabbing a disrespect for the מצוה, not a sign of love for it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he shall give', from the פסוק about the gifts

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule: a כהן must not grab his gifts. The rest of the sugya builds on it.

phrases.english: And I resolved it for him:
'And he shall give' means he shall not take by himself.
phrases.notes: דברים 18:3

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Grabbing is disrespectful, because the פסוק requires the owner to give.

steps.title: אביי stops grabbing and starts asking
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that at first he grabbed the gifts out of love for the מצוה. Once he heard ״וְנָתַן״, he stopped grabbing and asked for them instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: At first I used to grab the gifts. I thought I was showing love for the מצוה. Once I heard 'and he shall give, not take by himself', I stopped grabbing, and I would say: Give me.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי, a כהן, begins telling his personal story. This is the first stage, where he moves from grabbing to asking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His first reason for grabbing is exactly the 'love for the מצוה' side of רב יוסף's question. Once he learned the derivation from step 6, he changed what he did. Asking still lets the owner do the giving.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מֵרֵישׁ הֲוָה חָטֵיפְנָא מַתְּנָתָא,
phrases.english: Abaye said: At first I used to grab the gifts,
for I said: I am showing love for the מצוה.
Once I heard this teaching:
'and he shall give', and not that he take by himself,
I no longer grabbed,
but I would say: Give me.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording, 'I would say'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מֵרֵישׁ הֲוָה חָטֵיפְנָא מַתְּנָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the rule of step 6 being put into practice by a real כהן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grabbing is wrong. Asking is the first acceptable level.

steps.title: אביי stops asking and only accepts
steps.stepSummary: After hearing רבי מאיר's teaching that the sons of שמואל sinned by asking for their share, אביי stopped asking. He only took gifts when people offered them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And once I heard the ברייתא: 'They turned aside after money'. רבי מאיר says: The sons of שמואל asked for their portion with their mouths. Then I stopped asking too, but if they gave me, I took.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second stage of אביי's story. He learns that even asking is not proper, so he only accepts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק criticizes the sons of שמואל, and רבי מאיר explains that their sin was asking for their share out loud. So asking is also a lower level. Accepting what is offered is better.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They turned aside after money', said about the sons of שמואל

phrases.english: And once I heard that which is taught in a ברייתא:
'And they turned aside after money',
phrases.notes: שמואל א 8:3

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: בְּנֵי שְׁמוּאֵל חֶלְקָם שָׁאֲלוּ בְּפִיהֶם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: The sons of Shmuel asked for their portion with their mouths,
phrases.notes: The sons of שמואל were לויים, so their 'portion' was the gift owed to a לוי.

phrases.english: I no longer even said anything,
but if they gave to me, I would take.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן דִּשְׁמַעְנָא לְהָא דְּתַנְיָא: ״וַיִּטּוּ אַחֲרֵי הַבָּצַע״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the standard one more level, from asking to only accepting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Asking for the gifts is also improper. A pious כהן only accepts what is offered.

steps.title: אביי stops taking at all, except on ערב יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: After hearing that the modest כהנים hold back their hands, אביי stopped taking gifts at all. The exception was ערב יום כיפור, so that people would still know he was a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once I heard the ברייתא: 'The modest ones pull back their hands, and the greedy ones divide it up', I stopped taking as well. The only exception was ערב יום כיפור, so that I would keep my standing as a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the final stage of אביי's story. He stopped taking the gifts at all, with one exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא praises the כהנים who hold back and calls the ones who take everything greedy. So אביי gave up even accepting. He still took once a year, because a כהן who never takes gifts might be suspected of not really being a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: ערב יום כיפור, the day before יום כיפור
To keep myself established as a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: There are levels in receiving the מתנות: grabbing (forbidden), asking (not proper), accepting (allowed), and refusing (most modest). אביי still took once a year so his status as a כהן would stay clear.

phrases.english: Once I heard that which is taught in a ברייתא:
The modest ones pull back their hands,
phrases.notes: This ברייתא is about כהנים dividing holy bread among themselves.

phrases.english: and the greedy ones divide it up,
I no longer even took,
except on the eve of Yom Kippur,
to keep myself established among the priests.
phrases.notes: He means that if he never took gifts, people might start doubting he was really a כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דִּשְׁמַעְנָא לְהָא דְּתַנְיָא: הַצְּנוּעִים מוֹשְׁכִין אֶת יְדֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final and highest level of אביי's progression, with one exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The most modest כהן refuses the gifts, but takes them occasionally to keep his status as a כהן known.

steps.title: Why not show he is a כהן through ברכת כהנים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: אביי could have shown he was a כהן by saying ברכת כהנים. Why did he need to take gifts on ערב יום כיפור?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him spread his hands for ברכת כהנים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's reason for taking gifts on ערב יום כיפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His only reason for taking was to keep his status as a כהן known. Saying ברכת כהנים in public would do that just as well, so it seems he did not need to take gifts at all.

keyTerms.meaning: To spread his hands, meaning to say ברכת כהנים

phrases.english: But let him spread his hands!
phrases.notes: Let him go up and say ברכת כהנים, which shows everyone he is a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given at the end of step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reason for taking gifts on ערב יום כיפור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is another way to show he is a כהן that does not require taking gifts.

steps.title: אביי's schedule did not allow it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that אביי's schedule kept him from being in shul for ברכת כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: His time constrained him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. אביי could not regularly say ברכת כהנים because of his schedule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since ברכת כהנים was not available to him, taking gifts once a year was his only way to keep his status as a כהן known. So his practice in step 9 stands.

phrases.english: His schedule held him back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי could have shown he was a כהן through ברכת כהנים and did not need to take gifts.
steps.terutzMaskana: His schedule kept him from ברכת כהנים, so taking gifts on ערב יום כיפור was necessary.

steps.title: A כהן may give his future gifts to a poor Torah scholar
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that a כהן may give his expected מתנות to a needy תלמיד חכם in his neighborhood, even before he has received them, if he is a כהן with a fixed group of people who always give him their gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: If a כהן has a young Torah scholar living near him who is short of money, the כהן may give him the gifts. He may do this even though the gifts have not reached him yet, as long as he is a כהן whose regular people always give him their gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a new rule: a כהן may pass his מתנות to a poor תלמיד חכם, even before they reach him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you cannot give away something that is not yours yet. Here it works because this כהן is one of the מכרי כהונה: people always give him their gifts, so the gifts are as good as his. The goal is to help a תלמיד חכם who is struggling.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him give ownership (transfer the right to the gifts)
A כהן or לוי who has a regular group of people who always give him their gifts

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
This כהן who has
a young Torah scholar in his neighborhood,
and things are tight for him (he is short of money) –
let him give him ownership of the gifts,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא אָתֵי לִידֵיהּ,
phrases.english: and even though they have not yet come into his hands,
in a case of "acquaintances of כהונה and לויה."
phrases.notes: A כהן whose regular people always give him their gifts, so he can count on getting them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הַאי כָּהֲנָא דְּאִית לֵיהּ צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New ruling about the מתנות, after the stories about how אביי handled them
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who is one of the מכרי כהונה may give his expected gifts to a needy תלמיד חכם, even before they reach him.

steps.title: רבא asks the attendant to give him the gifts
steps.stepSummary: רבא and רב ספרא visit מר יוחנא, who serves them a choice calf. רבא asks the כהן attendant to give him the gifts because he wants tongue with mustard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא and רב ספרא visited the house of מר יוחנא, son of רב חנא בר אדא (some say son of רב חנא בר ביזנא). He prepared a choice calf for them. רבא said to the attendant: Give us the gifts, because I want to eat tongue with mustard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story that will test רב יוסף's rule. This step sets up the situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attendant was a כהן who would normally get the gifts from this host. רבא uses רב יוסף's rule and asks the attendant to hand them over. The tongue comes with the cheeks, which is one of the gifts, so he needs the attendant's permission to eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: A third-born calf, a choice, tender animal

phrases.english: Rava and Rav Safra happened to come

phrases.aramaic: לְבֵי מָר יוֹחָנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חָנָא בַּר אַדָּא,
phrases.english: to the house of Mar Yochana son of Rav Chana bar Adda,
and some say, to the house of Mar Yochana
son of Rav Chana bar Bizna.
He prepared for them a third-born calf,
Rava said to his attendant:
phrases.notes: The host's attendant was a כהן who usually received the gifts from him.

phrases.english: Give us ownership of the gifts,
because I want to eat tongue with mustard.
phrases.notes: The tongue comes along with the cheeks, which are one of the gifts.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא וְרַב סָפְרָא אִיקְּלַעוּ לְבֵי מָר יוֹחָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story where רבא acts on רב יוסף's rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא had the כהן attendant give him the gifts so he could eat them.

steps.title: רבא eats, רב ספרא holds back, and רב ספרא has a dream
steps.stepSummary: רבא eats the gifts but רב ספרא does not. Then רב ספרא is shown a troubling פסוק in a dream.
steps.simpleTranslation: The attendant gave him the gifts. רבא ate, and רב ספרא did not eat. In a dream they read to רב ספרא: "Like one who takes off a garment on a cold day, like vinegar on natron, so is one who sings songs to a troubled heart."
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on: the two rabbis act differently, and רב ספרא gets a worrying sign in a dream. This sets up his question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about something useless or harmful, which sounds like a rebuke. Since רב ספרא did not eat, it is not clear what he did wrong. That confusion leads him to ask רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: They read it to him in a dream
Vinegar on natron (a mix that ruins it)

phrases.english: He gave him ownership.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אֲכַל, וְרַב סָפְרָא לָא אֲכַל.
phrases.english: Rava ate, and Rav Safra did not eat.
They read to Rav Safra in a dream:
"Like one who takes off a garment on a cold day,
phrases.notes: משלי 25:20

phrases.english: vinegar on natron,
and one who sings songs to a troubled heart."

steps.triggerLanguage: זַכִּי לֵיהּ. רָבָא אֲכַל, וְרַב סָפְרָא לָא אֲכַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story and shows the two rabbis acting differently
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא ate the gifts, רב ספרא did not, and רב ספרא was shown a worrying פסוק in a dream.

steps.title: רב ספרא asks רב יוסף if he did wrong
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא asks רב יוסף whether the dream came because he did not follow רב יוסף's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רב יוסף and said to him: Maybe they read me this because I went against the Master's teaching?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא asks רב יוסף directly whether refusing to eat was a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ספרא worries that by not eating, he acted as if רב יוסף's rule was wrong. He asks the person who made the rule to explain what it really covers.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף, אֲמַר לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: He came before Rav Yosef and said to him:
Perhaps because I went against
the teaching of the Master
they read me this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב ספרא reacts to the dream by asking about the rule
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Was it wrong not to eat, given רב יוסף's ruling?

steps.title: רב יוסף explains two limits on his rule
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says רב ספרא was right. His rule only works when the כהן gives freely, and only for someone who really needs it. An attendant gives under pressure, and רבא could afford his own meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: When I said it, I meant a כהן giving to another person by his own choice. An attendant gives against his will. And when I said it, I meant for someone who has no other way. But this one did have another way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers that רב ספרא did nothing wrong, because this case does not fit his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two limits. First, an attendant feels pressure from his boss's guests, so he does not truly give willingly. Second, the rule was for a poor תלמיד חכם, but רבא could have bought his own meat.

keyTerms.meaning: With someone else (a person the כהן chooses on his own)
He has no other way (he cannot afford it)

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's rule has two conditions: the כהן must give willingly, and the תלמיד חכם must really be in need. In the story both conditions were missing, so רב ספרא was right not to eat.
steps.confusionAlert: The dream was not because רב ספרא did wrong. רב יוסף tells him his holding back was correct.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כִּי אֲמַרִי אֲנָא – בְּאַחֵר,
phrases.english: He said to him: When I said it, it was about another person,
phrases.notes: He means a כהן giving to someone he chose on his own, without anyone pushing him.

phrases.english: but an attendant gives ownership against his will,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי אֲמַרִי אֲנָא – לְמַאן דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: and when I said it, it was for someone who has no other way,
but this one did have another way.
phrases.notes: רבא was not poor, so he could have bought his own meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲמַרִי אֲנָא – בְּאַחֵר, שַׁמָּעָא – בְּעַל כֻּרְחֵיהּ מְזַכֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ספרא's question and narrows רב יוסף's rule
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב ספרא did not go against the rule. The rule only applies when the כהן gives willingly to someone of his choice, and only for a needy person. Here the attendant was pressured and רבא was not needy.

steps.title: Then why was I shown that verse?
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא asks: if I acted correctly, why was I shown a troubling פסוק?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what is the reason they read this verse to me?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא has just heard that he acted correctly by not eating the gifts. Now he asks why he was shown a frightening פסוק in his dream at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15 רב ספרא assumed the dream was a punishment for not following רב יוסף's ruling. רב יוסף said he acted properly, so that explanation no longer works. The dream now needs a new explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: They read to me / they showed me (a פסוק, in a dream)

phrases.english: But then, what is the reason
that they read this to me?
phrases.notes: "This" is the troubling פסוק he was shown in the dream back in step 14.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from רב יוסף's answer that רב ספרא acted correctly, which leaves the dream unexplained.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why was רב ספרא shown the troubling פסוק if he did nothing wrong?

steps.title: The verse was aimed at רבא
steps.stepSummary: The dream was directed toward רבא, not toward רב ספרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was directed toward רבא!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers that the פסוק was not about רב ספרא at all. It was a message about רבא, who ate the gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dream was a message, but רב ספרא was not its target. It criticized רבא, who took the gifts even though he did not really need them.

phrases.english: It was toward רבא!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ספרא's question about the dream.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק was a message aimed at רבא, who ate the gifts improperly.

steps.title: Why not show it to רבא himself?
steps.stepSummary: If the message was for רבא, the dream should have been shown to רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let them read it to רבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If רבא was the one who did wrong, why didn't he get the dream himself?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a message from heaven goes to the person it concerns. Sending רבא's warning to רב ספרא seems strange.

keyTerms.meaning: So let them read it (to him)

phrases.english: So let them read it to רבא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the dream was aimed at רבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A message meant for רבא should have come to רבא directly, not to רב ספרא.

steps.title: רבא was under a rebuke
steps.stepSummary: רבא was rebuked, so he did not receive heavenly messages. That is why רב ספרא was shown the פסוק instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא was under a rebuke.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Because of this incident, רבא was under a rebuke from heaven, so the message could not come to him directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who is נזוף is held at a distance and does not get messages from heaven. So the message went to the person sitting next to him, רב ספרא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rebuked, held at a distance (here, by heaven)

steps.whatToRemember: The dream was really a criticism of רבא. רב ספרא acted correctly; he was only shown the פסוק because רבא was under a rebuke.

phrases.english: רבא was under a rebuke.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the normal expectation did not apply in this case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dream should have gone to רבא himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא was rebuked and could not receive the message, so it was shown to רב ספרא.

steps.title: What does the verse simply mean?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב דימי what the dream פסוק means in its plain sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב דימי: The plain meaning of the verse, what is it written about?
steps.whatsHappening: The story is over. Now אביי asks about the פסוק itself: apart from this dream, what is it simply talking about?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dream used the פסוק as a hint about רבא. אביי wants its basic, simple meaning, apart from the dream. The next step gives that meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: The plain meaning of the פסוק

phrases.english: אביי said to רב דימי:
And the plain meaning of the verse, what is it written about?
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק from the dream: משלי 25:20.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story to the simple meaning of the פסוק used in the dream.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The plain meaning of the dream פסוק

steps.title: It is about teaching an unworthy student
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי says the פסוק is about someone who teaches Torah to an unworthy student.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is about one who teaches an unworthy student.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers that, in its plain meaning, the פסוק criticizes teaching Torah to a student who is not fit for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as singing songs to a heavy heart does no good, teaching Torah to a student who will not live by it is wasted. רב דימי is giving the פסוק's own simple meaning, apart from how the dream used it.

phrases.english: He said to him:
About one who teaches an unworthy student.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק is about teaching Torah to an unworthy student.

steps.title: Teaching an unworthy student leads to גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that whoever teaches an unworthy student falls into גיהנם, learned from a פסוק in איוב. The word שריד there means a תלמיד חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Anyone who teaches an unworthy student falls into גיהנם, as it says, "All darkness is hidden for his treasures; a fire not blown shall consume him; it will go badly for the שריד in his tent." And שריד means only a תלמיד חכם, as it says, "And among the remnant (שרידים) whom ה׳ calls."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב דימי with a teaching of רב: teaching Torah to an unworthy student is so serious that the teacher falls into גיהנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in איוב speaks of a consuming fire, which is read as גיהנם, and of a שריד who is bad (ירע). Since שריד means a תלמיד חכם, a "bad תלמיד חכם" is an unworthy student. The fire is the punishment for the one who taught him.

keyTerms.meaning: Remnant, survivor; here read as a תלמיד חכם

steps.confusionAlert: The fire is the punishment for the teacher. The unworthy student is only the one being described by the words "ירע שריד" (a bad scholar).

phrases.english: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב:
Anyone who teaches an unworthy student
falls into גיהנם,
as it says, "All darkness is hidden away for his treasures,
phrases.notes: איוב 20:26

phrases.english: a fire not blown will consume him,
it will go badly for the שריד in his tent,"
phrases.notes: ירע sounds like רע, "bad," so it's read as "a bad scholar," meaning the unworthy student.

phrases.english: and שריד means nothing other than a תלמיד חכם,
as it says, "And among the remnant whom ה׳ calls."
phrases.notes: יואל 3:5

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב דימי's claim that teaching an unworthy student is a serious wrong.
steps.raayaObject: That teaching an unworthy student is a grave wrong
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's teaching based on איוב 20:26 and יואל 3:5

steps.title: Like throwing a stone to מרקוליס
steps.stepSummary: רב also teaches that teaching an unworthy student is like throwing a stone to the idol מרקוליס, based on two פסוקים in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רב: Anyone who teaches an unworthy student is like one who throws a stone to מרקוליס, as it says, "Like a pebble in a heap of stones, so is one who gives honor to a fool." And it is written, "Luxury is not fitting for a fool."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רב on the same topic. It compares teaching an unworthy student to a form of idol worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרקוליס was worshipped by throwing stones onto its heap. The פסוק says giving honor to a fool is like adding a stone to such a heap. The second פסוק adds that good things are not fitting for a fool.

keyTerms.meaning: An idol worshipped by throwing stones at it

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק from רב ספרא's dream is, in its plain meaning, about teaching an unworthy student. רב treats this very harshly: such a teacher falls into גיהנם, and it is like throwing a stone to מרקוליס.
steps.whyThisMatters: Together with step 23, this shows how seriously רב views teaching Torah to an unworthy student. This is the plain meaning of the פסוק that רב ספרא was shown in his dream.

phrases.english: רבי זירא said in the name of רב:
Anyone who teaches an unworthy student
is like one who throws a stone to מרקוליס,
phrases.notes: מרקוליס was an idol people worshipped by throwing stones onto its pile.

phrases.english: as it says, "Like a pebble in a heap of stones,
phrases.notes: משלי 26:8

phrases.english: so is one who gives honor to a fool,"
and it is written, "Luxury is not fitting for a fool."
phrases.notes: משלי 19:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second teaching of רב on teaching an unworthy student.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teaching an unworthy student is like throwing a stone to מרקוליס.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: a partner must mark, even with a גוי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a partner of a כהן or a גוי must mark the animal, and wonders whether this really applies even to a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one who enters into partnership with them (a כהן or a גוי) must mark the animal. And is that true even with a גוי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה and asks a surprised question about it. This sets up the next step, where it will bring a source that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה puts the כהן and the גוי together: a partner of either one must mark the animal. The גמרא is surprised that the rule covers a גוי too. That surprise is the opening for the contradiction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One who enters into a partnership (here, a partnership in an animal)
To mark, to put a sign on it so people know the animal is shared
And even, showing surprise that the rule stretches this far

phrases.english: And one who enters into partnership with them
phrases.notes: "Them" means the כהן and the גוי that the משנה just mentioned.

phrases.english: must mark [the animal],
And even with a gentile?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַמִּשְׁתַּתֵּף עִמָּהֶן צָרִיךְ לִרְשׁוֹם, וַאֲפִילּוּ עִם הַגּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about teaching an unworthy student and returns to the משנה's law about marking a shared animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה rules that a partner of a כהן or a גוי must mark the animal. The גמרא questions whether this really includes a גוי.

steps.title: A ברייתא says there is no need to mark with a גוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a partner of a כהן must mark, but a partner of a גוי, and one with פסולי המוקדשים, does not need to mark. This contradicts the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they raised a contradiction: one who partners with a כהן must mark. But one who partners with a גוי, and one with disqualified consecrated animals, does not need to mark!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets a ברייתא against the משנה. The ברייתא says a partner of a גוי does not need to mark, while the משנה says he does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources agree about the כהן: his partner must mark. They clash only about the גוי. The משנה includes the גוי, but the ברייתא puts the גוי together with פסולי המוקדשים, where no marking is needed. The גמרא must now explain how both can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: And they set them against each other. This introduces a contradiction between two sources.
Consecrated animals that became disqualified for the מזבח and were redeemed

steps.confusionAlert: The contradiction is only about the גוי. About the כהן, the משנה and the ברייתא agree that one must mark.

phrases.english: And they raise a contradiction:
One who enters into partnership with a priest must mark [the animal],
but one who enters into partnership with a gentile
and [one who slaughters] disqualified consecrated animals
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets aren't in the Hebrew; they just fill in what the ברייתא means.

phrases.english: does not need to mark [the animal]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the surprise in step 25: a ברייתא that disagrees with the משנה about the גוי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a partner of a גוי must mark the animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says outright that a partner of a גוי does not need to mark, which directly contradicts the משנה.
